label: Surf
blurb: Famous breaks for every level, from beginner beach breaks to big-wave reefs.
sources: WSL championship tour and challenger venues

places.name: Mavericks
places.why: A cold-water freight-train reef that only turns on with big NW winter swell; several surfers have died here.

places.name: Steamer Lane
places.why: A rock-ledge point off a lighthouse point, breaking rights across several take-off zones; classic and crowded.

places.name: Ocean Beach
places.why: Heavy, shifting beach-break peaks with strong rips and cold water; for experienced surfers only.

places.name: Rincon
places.why: The 'Queen of the Coast' point, long peeling right walls over cobblestone on a good NW swell.

places.name: Malibu (Surfrider Beach)
places.why: Three connecting longboard-friendly point sections that made California surf culture famous; packed most days.

places.name: Lower Trestles
places.why: A cobblestone-bottom point-reef with rippable rights and lefts; hosts the WSL Finals for its consistency.

places.name: Huntington Beach Pier
places.why: Punchy, consistent beach-break peaks either side of the pier; hosts the US Open of Surfing.

places.name: Blacks Beach
places.why: A steep, powerful beach-break under the Torrey Pines cliffs, known for hollow, punishing close-outs.

places.name: The Wedge
places.why: A jetty-refracted freak wave that doubles up into a huge, square barrel; famous and dangerous for bodysurfers.

places.name: Swami's
places.why: A user-friendly reef point below a clifftop meditation garden, with a long, workable right wall.

places.name: Pipeline
places.why: The world's most famous barrel: a shallow reef that turns winter swell into thick, hollow, dangerous lefts.

places.name: Waimea Bay
places.why: The spot that started big-wave surfing; only breaks on major NW swells over 20 feet Hawaiian.

places.name: Sunset Beach
places.why: A shifting, powerful reef break famous for peaky, unpredictable rights that punish poor positioning.

places.name: Jaws (Peʻahi)
places.why: A deep-water reef that stands up into some of the tallest rideable waves on earth; tow-in and paddle big-wave venue.

places.name: Honolua Bay
places.why: A long, mechanical right point inside a marine reserve bay, considered one of the best right points in the world.

places.name: Waikiki
places.why: Gentle, rolling reef and beach waves where modern surfing was popularized; crowded with beginners and canoes.

places.name: Hanalei Bay
places.why: A scenic bay with several peaks from mellow beginner rollers to a solid outer reef on bigger swells.

places.name: Tres Palmas
places.why: A big-wave reef inside a marine reserve, the Caribbean's premier winter swell magnet.

places.name: Zicatela Beach
places.why: The 'Mexican Pipeline': a brutally powerful, hollow beach-break shorebreak for experienced surfers only.

places.name: Pascuales
places.why: An extremely heavy, shallow beach-break barrel that has broken boards and backs; not for the timid.

places.name: Sayulita
places.why: A mellow, forgiving beach and point break that has become Mexico's go-to learner town.

places.name: Killers, Isla Todos Santos
places.why: A big-wave reef off an island south of Ensenada, one of the best cold-water big-wave spots in North America.

places.name: Punta Mita
places.why: A gentle, long-running point wave over sand and rock, ideal for building confidence past whitewater.

places.name: Pavones
places.why: One of the longest lefts in the world, a river-mouth point that can run for well over a kilometre on a good swell.

places.name: Santa Teresa
places.why: A stretch of consistent beach-break peaks that suits everyone from first-timers to experienced surfers.

places.name: Salsa Brava
places.region: Puerto Viejo de Talamanca, Costa Rica
places.why: A shallow coral reef producing the Caribbean side's heaviest, most dangerous wave.

places.name: Popoyo
places.why: A hollow, powerful A-frame reef-and-beach setup that put Nicaragua's offshore-blessed coast on the map.

places.name: El Sunzal
places.why: A friendly, rippable right point that made El Salvador a growing warm-water destination.

places.name: Punta Roca
places.why: El Salvador's best-known point, a long, powerful right that hosted the ISA World Surfing Games.

places.name: Santa Catalina
places.why: A punchy, hollow point and reef combo facing the open Pacific, a launchpad for Coiba boat trips.

places.name: Playa Hermosa
places.why: A powerful, consistent beach-break that hosted world-tour events and rewards strong paddling.

places.name: Chicama
places.why: The longest left-hand point wave in the world, with rides claimed to run over two kilometres.

places.name: Pico Alto
places.why: Peru's premier big-wave reef, a heavy right that only breaks on the biggest south swells.

places.name: Punta Rocas
places.why: A long, powerful right point-reef that has hosted WSL Challenger Series events.

places.name: Cabo Blanco
places.why: A rocky point made famous when Hemingway fished nearby, still producing long, fast right walls.

places.name: Máncora
places.why: A warm, easy point wave that anchors Peru's most popular beginner-friendly surf town.

places.name: Praia da Joaquina
places.why: Brazil's best-known beach-break, a consistent sandbar setup with regular national contests.

places.name: Praia da Tiririca
places.why: A rivermouth point wrapped by rainforest, offering long, workable walls in warm water.

places.name: Cacimba do Padre
places.why: A powerful reef-and-beach wave on a remote volcanic archipelago, punchy on the seasonal south swell.

places.name: Itaúna Beach
places.why: Brazil's most consistent heavy beach-break, home to a long-running WSL Challenger Series stop.

places.name: Maresias Beach
places.why: A lively, punchy beach-break popular with Brazil's competitive surf scene.

places.name: Punta de Lobos
places.why: A rocky point that throws up long, powerful lefts and doubles as a big-wave tow venue in size.

places.name: Montañita
places.why: A friendly beach and point wave at the centre of Ecuador's most popular surf town.

places.name: La Barra
places.why: A rivermouth-influenced beach and point setup that anchors Uruguay's small surf scene.

places.name: Praia do Norte
places.why: A submarine canyon focuses swell into the biggest rideable waves ever surfed, tow and paddle big-wave surfing.

places.name: Supertubos
places.why: One of Europe's heaviest beach-break barrels, host to a WSL Championship Tour event.

places.name: Coxos
places.why: A world-class right reef break inside Europe's first World Surfing Reserve.

places.name: Ribeira d'Ilhas
places.why: A long, consistent right point-reef that has hosted world-tour events for decades.

places.name: Carcavelos
places.why: Lisbon's easy-access beach-break, the region's default learner and longboard spot.

places.name: Arrifana
places.why: A scenic reef-point below dramatic cliffs on Portugal's wild southwest coast.

places.name: Praia do Amado
places.why: A wide, forgiving beach-break that hosts Algarve surf schools year-round.

places.name: Mundaka
places.why: A rivermouth sandbar point producing one of Europe's best barrelling lefts, WSL tour history.

places.name: Zarautz
places.why: A long, sandy beach-break that is the Basque coast's most popular learner and longboard spot.

places.name: El Palmar
places.why: An open, consistent Atlantic beach-break south of Cádiz, popular with schools.

places.name: Playa de Somo
places.why: A wide sandy beach-break across the bay from Santander, Cantabria's surf hub.

places.name: Playa de Pantín
places.why: A powerful, consistent Galician beach-break that has hosted a long-running WQS/QS contest.

places.name: Playa de Las Canteras
places.why: A reef-protected city beach with a gentle inside section for beginners and a punchier outer bank.

places.name: El Quemao
places.why: A shallow, ledging left reef that becomes a serious big-wave venue on large north Atlantic swells.

places.name: La Gravière
places.why: A shifting sandbank beach-break that produces some of Europe's heaviest, most hollow barrels.

places.name: Lafitenia
places.why: A rocky point break giving the Basque coast's longest, most consistent right wall.

places.name: Guéthary
places.why: A powerful reef point that turns on with size, one of the French coast's heaviest waves.

places.name: Côte des Basques
places.why: The birthplace of French surfing, a beach-break under the villa-lined cliffs, crowded and beginner-friendly.

places.name: La Torche
places.why: Brittany's most famous beach-break, a punchy peak below a distinctive headland.

places.name: Belharra
places.why: A deep-water reef offshore that only wakes up on huge Atlantic swells, tow-surfed by big-wave specialists.

places.name: Fistral Beach
places.why: England's best-known beach-break, a consistent, contest-hosting sandbar strip.

places.name: Croyde Bay
places.why: A punchy, powerful beach-break packed between two headlands, heavier than it looks.

places.name: Bantham Beach
places.why: A rivermouth beach-break with a sandbar that produces some of Devon's best shape.

places.name: Thurso East
places.why: A cold, world-class righthand reef point below a castle, one of Europe's best cold-water waves.

places.name: Lahinch
places.why: A forgiving beach-break that anchors Ireland's most established surf town, with reefs nearby for more power.

places.name: The Peak, Bundoran
places.why: A reliable reef-point that put Ireland's Atlantic coast on the surfing map.

places.name: Easkey Right
places.why: A classic righthand point over rock ledges, one of Ireland's original surf discoveries.

places.name: Mullaghmore Head
places.why: A slabbing reef off a rugged headland that became one of the world's great cold-water big-wave venues.

places.name: Unstad Beach
places.why: An Arctic beach-break inside a dramatic fjord, surfed in drysuits under the midnight sun or northern lights.

places.name: Anchor Point
places.why: A long, mechanical right point that put Morocco's south coast on the world surf map.

places.name: Imsouane Bay
places.why: One of the longest right points in Africa, a gentle wrap into a working fishing bay, great for progression.

places.name: Garden Reef
places.why: A fast, hollow righthand reef break next to Safi's harbour, one of Morocco's most powerful waves.

places.name: Ngor Right
places.why: A reef-point off a small island suburb of Dakar, West Africa's best-known wave.

places.name: Fisherman's Point
places.why: A long right point wave that reopened Liberia's surf coast to the world after decades of war.

places.name: Busua Beach
places.why: A relaxed beach-break that anchors Ghana's small but growing surf scene.

places.name: Cabo Ledo
places.why: A long, uncrowded right point on Angola's sparsely surfed coast.

places.name: Supertubes
places.why: A world-famous righthand point delivering long, fast, perfectly shaped walls, WSL Championship Tour venue.

places.name: Dungeons
places.why: A cold, shark-rich big-wave reef off the Cape Peninsula, tow and paddle venue for the Cape Town big-wave crew.

places.name: Muizenberg Beach
places.why: A gentle, sandy beach-break in a scenic bay, South Africa's default learner spot.

places.name: Nahoon Reef
places.why: A powerful righthand reef break known for testing world-tour-level surfers.

places.name: Elands Bay
places.why: A cold, long lefthand point on South Africa's west coast, powerful and often uncrowded.

places.name: Victoria Bay
places.why: A small, sheltered bay point that is one of South Africa's most reliable beginner waves.

places.name: Cave Rock
places.why: A punchy reef break next to Durban's harbour mouth, a local proving ground.

places.name: Skeleton Bay
places.why: A freak sandbar point in the desert that produces some of the longest, most perfect barrels on earth.

places.name: Ponta do Ouro
places.why: A warm-water point-and-reef setup near the South African border, uncrowded and consistent.

places.name: St-Leu
places.why: A long, fast lefthand reef point, one of the Indian Ocean's best waves though shark-restricted.

places.name: Tamarin Bay
places.why: A hollow lefthand reef known locally as 'Tombant', Mauritius's premier wave.

places.name: Uluwatu
places.why: A long limestone cave-lined reef with multiple sections firing on the dry-season swell, Bali's signature wave.

places.name: Padang Padang
places.why: A short, intense, world-class lefthand barrel over a shallow reef shelf.

places.name: Bingin
places.why: A fast, hollow lefthand reef beneath a cliffside village, one of the Bukit Peninsula's most photographed waves.

places.name: Balangan
places.why: A rippable lefthand reef point that offers a gentler alternative to its Bukit Peninsula neighbours.

places.name: Keramas
places.why: A powerful righthand beach-and-reef wave that has hosted WSL Championship Tour events.

places.name: Canggu (Batu Bolong)
places.why: A lively beach-break scene with several peaks, now Bali's most crowded surf-and-cafe hub.

places.name: Kuta Beach
places.why: Bali's original beginner beach-break, gentle whitewater and a full strip of surf schools.

places.name: Desert Point
places.why: One of the world's longest, most perfect lefthand barrels, breaking over shallow reef into a lagoon.

places.name: Ekas
places.why: A powerful righthand reef inside a remote bay on Lombok's south coast.

places.name: G-Land (Plengkung)
places.why: A long, world-class lefthand reef inside a national park jungle, reached only by boat.

places.name: Lakey Peak
places.why: A powerful A-frame reef-point offering both a long right and a short, punchy left.

places.name: Lagundri Bay
places.why: A near-perfect righthand point wave that was one of the original Indonesian surf discoveries of the 1970s.

places.name: Macaronis
places.why: A flawless, clinical lefthand reef, the signature wave of the Mentawai boat-charter scene.

places.name: Cloud 9
places.why: A powerful, hollow righthand reef barrel that made Siargao the Philippines' surf capital.

places.name: Main Point
places.why: A long, forgiving righthand point wave, the anchor of Sri Lanka's east-coast surf scene.

places.name: Hikkaduwa
places.why: A reef-and-beach combo that has hosted travelling surfers since the 1970s hippie trail.

places.name: Kovalam Beach
places.why: A mellow beach-break that anchors India's small but growing homegrown surf scene.

places.name: Sultans
places.why: A long righthand reef break over a shallow lagoon, one of the Maldives' original charter-boat waves.

places.name: Pasta Point
places.why: A fast lefthand reef reserved for guests of the island resort beside it.

places.name: Kugenuma Beach
places.why: A consistent beach-break close to Tokyo, Japan's most crowded weekend surf spot.

places.name: Isumi
places.why: A stretch of beach-breaks on the Pacific-facing Chiba coast, venue for the Tokyo Olympics surfing.

places.name: Mui Ne
places.why: A seasonal beach-break that is Vietnam's best-known, if inconsistent, surf spot.

places.name: Riyue Bay
places.why: China's most developed surf beach, a sheltered bay with a dedicated surf-school strip.

places.name: Bells Beach
places.why: Australia's most historic wave, a powerful righthand point-reef and the world's longest-running pro contest site.

places.name: Winki Pop
places.why: A fast, high-performance reef break next door to Bells, favoured when Bells is too fat.

places.name: Snapper Rocks
places.why: The start of the Superbank, a sand-filled point that can link three breaks into an epic long right.

places.name: Kirra
places.why: A once-legendary sand-bottom point famous for long, deep barrels, still firing on the right swell.

places.name: Burleigh Heads
places.why: A rocky point wrapping around a headland reserve, producing long, hollow rights.

places.name: Noosa First Point
places.why: A gentle, scenic point wave inside a national park, one of Australia's best learner-to-intermediate waves.

places.name: The Pass
places.region: Byron Bay, New South Wales, Australia
places.why: A long, easy righthand point that is one of Australia's most crowded and beloved beginner-to-intermediate waves.

places.name: Lennox Head
places.why: A powerful righthand point below a headland, one of NSW's best when the swell is big.

places.name: Angourie Point
places.why: A classic rock-bottom right point and Australia's first officially declared National Surfing Reserve.

places.name: Crescent Head
places.why: A long, easy righthand point that has been a byword for longboarding since the 1960s.

places.name: North Narrabeen
places.why: A sand-and-rock point at a lagoon mouth that has produced generations of Australian world-tour surfers.

places.name: Bondi Beach
places.why: Australia's most famous city beach-break, patrolled and packed but a solid all-round wave.

places.name: Manly Beach
places.why: A wide, forgiving city beach-break, Sydney's other classic learner spot across the harbour.

places.name: Margaret River Main Break
places.why: A powerful reef break off a rivermouth, the centrepiece of Western Australia's world-tour venue.

places.name: The Right
places.why: A savage slab reef that only breaks a handful of days a year, among the heaviest waves on the planet.

places.name: Cactus Beach
places.why: A remote outpost with several reef and point setups, long a pilgrimage for travelling surfers.

places.name: Shipstern Bluff
places.why: A freakish, ledging slab beneath sea cliffs, reachable only by boat or a long hike, a big-wave test piece.

places.name: Cyclops
places.why: An extremely shallow, thick slab reef considered one of the heaviest waves in Australia.

places.name: Manu Bay
places.why: A long, mechanical left point made famous in the 1966 surf film 'The Endless Summer'.

places.name: Piha Beach
places.why: A black volcanic-sand beach-break with strong rips, Auckland's most iconic surf beach.

places.name: Shipwreck Bay
places.why: A long lefthand point at the southern end of Ninety Mile Beach, one of the North Island's best.

places.name: Mount Maunganui
places.why: A beach-and-point setup beside an extinct volcano, one of the North Island's most popular surf towns.

places.name: Cloudbreak
places.why: A world-class lefthand reef that breaks in several stages from a rippable wall to a serious big-wave barrel.

places.name: Restaurants
places.why: A short, hollow righthand reef opposite Cloudbreak, favoured for its shorter, punchier barrels.

places.name: Namotu Lefts
places.why: A playful, high-performance lefthand reef off Namotu Island, popular with visiting pros.

places.name: Teahupoʻo
places.why: An impossibly thick, glassy lefthand reef barrel over a shallow coral shelf, an Olympic and WSL venue.

places.name: Taapuna
places.why: A fast, punchy reef pass close to Tahiti's capital, popular with the local pro scene.

places.name: Soup Bowl
places.why: A powerful righthand reef on Barbados's rugged east coast, the Caribbean's best-known wave.

places.name: Boston Bay
places.why: A reef-and-point wave near the birthplace of jerk cooking, Jamaica's best-known surf spot.

places.name: Playa Encuentro
places.why: A consistent reef-and-beach break that anchors the Caribbean's most active surf town.

places.name: Surfer's Beach
places.why: A reef-and-point wave that draws a small, devoted crew to an otherwise quiet island.

places.name: Rockaway Beach
places.why: New York City's own beach-break, a hurricane-season sandbar wave a subway ride from Manhattan.

places.name: Montauk (Lighthouse/Ditch Plains)
places.why: A rock-reef point off Long Island's tip, the Northeast's best-known surf town wave.

places.name: Cocoa Beach
places.why: A gentle, consistent beach-break beside the Kennedy Space Center, Florida's surf capital.

places.name: Long Beach
places.why: A cold-water beach-break inside a national park reserve, Canada's most established surf town.

places.name: Lawrencetown Beach
places.why: A cold Atlantic beach-break that anchors Nova Scotia's small, hardy surf community.

places.name: Cardiff Reef
places.why: A mellow, forgiving reef point that is one of San Diego County's most popular learn-to-surf spots.

places.name: San Onofre
places.why: Slow-rolling longboard waves over a cobblestone bottom, a laid-back classic since the 1930s.

places.name: Haleiwa
places.why: A rivermouth point-reef at the west end of the North Shore, hosting the Vans Triple Crown opener.

places.name: Ala Moana Bowls
places.why: A hollow lefthand reef break within sight of Waikiki's high-rises, a high-performance local favourite.

places.name: Ghost Trees
places.why: A big-wave reef off the Monterey Peninsula's cypress-lined coast, tow-surfed on huge NW swells.

places.name: Windansea Beach
places.why: A rocky reef break with a tight local crew and a rustic surf shack landmark, one of San Diego's most iconic waves.

places.name: Linda Mar (Pacifica State Beach)
places.why: A sheltered, sandy beach-break that is the Bay Area's default learn-to-surf beach.

places.name: C Street (Surfer's Point)
places.why: A long, easy point wave beside a bike path, a reliable beginner-to-intermediate wave.

places.name: Salt Creek
places.why: A rocky point-reef producing punchy peaks, a longtime pro-am contest site.

places.name: Cape Hatteras
places.why: An exposed sandbar beach-break that catches hurricane swell along the Atlantic seaboard's best surf coast.

places.name: Domes
places.why: A rippable reef point next to a decommissioned nuclear dome, Rincón's most popular wave.

places.name: Off the Wall
places.why: A shallow, hollow reef break just east of Pipeline, favoured by locals for its speed and power.

places.name: Rocky Point
places.why: A playful multi-peak reef break popular for its shorter, more forgiving walls than its North Shore neighbours.

places.name: Velzyland
places.why: A tight, hollow righthand reef at the North Shore's quieter east end.

places.name: Hoʻokipa Beach Park
places.why: A reef point better known for windsurfing but also a serious, powerful surf wave on its day.

places.name: Poipu Beach
places.why: A gentle, sheltered beach popular with beginner surfers and snorkelers alike.

places.name: La Ticla
places.why: A rivermouth point wave on a remote stretch of the Michoacán coast.

places.name: San Miguel
places.why: A cobblestone point near the US border producing long, workable rights.

places.name: Playa Colorado
places.why: A powerful righthand point and beach combo on Nicaragua's offshore-blessed southern coast.

places.name: Playa Venao
places.why: A crescent bay beach-break that has grown into Panama's most popular surf town.

places.name: Playa Maderas
places.why: A reliable, punchy beach-break a short boat ride from San Juan del Sur.

places.name: Playa El Tunco
places.why: A rocky point-and-beach wave that anchors El Salvador's backpacker surf scene.

places.name: Playa El Zonte
places.why: A beginner-friendly point and beach break that grew up around El Salvador's 'Bitcoin Beach' scene.

places.name: Playa Grande
places.why: A wide, consistent beach-break beside a leatherback turtle nesting refuge.

places.name: Lobitos
places.why: A left point wave beside old oil-town piers, one of northern Peru's best waves.

places.name: Guarda do Embaú
places.why: A rivermouth point-and-beach setup near Florianópolis, popular with Brazilian surfers.

places.name: Praia Grande
places.why: A big, punchy beach-break beneath dramatic cliffs, popular with Lisbon surf schools and bodyboarders.

places.name: Baleal
places.why: A sheltered, sandy beach-break that is Peniche's default learner spot beside its heavier reefs.

places.name: Praia do Cabedelo
places.why: A rivermouth beach-break at the mouth of the Lima river, one of northern Portugal's best banks.

places.name: Playa de Rodiles
places.why: A rivermouth beach-break inside a protected estuary, Asturias's best-known wave.

places.name: Playa de Salinas
places.why: A long sandy beach-break that hosts Spain's national surf championships.

places.name: Les Bourdaines
places.why: A hollow, high-performance beach-break just north of Hossegor's banks.

places.name: Watergate Bay
places.why: A wide, gently sloping beach popular with schools north of Fistral.

places.name: Porthleven
places.why: A heavy, hollow righthand reef next to a historic harbour, one of England's most powerful waves.

places.name: Strandhill
places.why: A popular beach-break with a strong surf-school scene beneath Knocknarea mountain.

places.name: Inch Beach
places.why: A vast, gently shelving beach on the Wild Atlantic Way, forgiving for beginners.

places.name: Sidi Kaouki
places.why: A wide, windswept beach-and-point wave south of Essaouira, popular with kite and surf schools alike.

places.name: Mirleft
places.why: A cluster of uncrowded points and reefs on Morocco's remote southern coast.

places.name: Llandudno Beach
places.why: A steep, powerful shorebreak beneath granite boulders on the Cape Peninsula's Atlantic side.

places.name: Bruce's Beauties
places.why: The point that gave 'The Endless Summer' its final wave, a long, glassy right.

places.name: Green Bowl
places.why: A remote reef break reached down a long staircase, less crowded than its Bukit neighbours.

places.name: Shipwrecks
places.why: A powerful righthand reef pass off a small island east of Bali, a favourite fast-boat day trip.

places.name: Batu Karas
places.why: A sheltered bay with both a mellow beach-break and a longer point, popular with learners and boat-trippers alike.

places.name: Impossibles
places.why: A long, fast lefthand reef between Padang Padang and Bingin, rippable at multiple sections.

places.name: Jinzun Harbor
places.why: A harbour-wall point wave and the training base for Taiwan's national surf team.

places.name: Yallingup
places.why: A scenic reef break inside a sheltered bay, one of the region's most photogenic waves.

places.name: Tombstones
places.why: A remote, heavy reef break on an outback pastoral station, a big-wave test far from any town.

places.name: Merewether Beach
places.why: A consistent city beach-break beside Australia's largest ocean baths.

places.name: Wainui Beach
places.why: A long, consistent beach-break that has produced more world-tour surfers per capita than anywhere in New Zealand.

places.name: Whangamata Bar
places.why: A rivermouth sandbar producing one of the North Island's best righthand barrels.
